title: Fallback profile calibration and cost-quality tuning checklist
body:
Purpose:
Short notes / checklist to calibrate cheaper inference profiles (quantized/shorter-context variants / distilled variants) against quality gates and estimate cost upside/downside. This is intentionally pragmatic — half spreadsheet, half experimental playbook so engineers and PMs can run reps and lock gate thresholds before rollouts.

High-level objective:
- Define automated quality gates for cheaper configs that protect absolute/relative quality for production prompts while enabling measurable cost savings.
- Provide a repeatable spreadsheet-backed calibration procedure teams can run weekly when adding a new cheap profile.

Important definitions (for this doc):
- baseline: current production model/profile (full float / full KV cache).
- cheap_profile: any configuration that reduces unit cost (e.g., 4-bit quant, shorter context, distilled model).
- eval_set: representative set of 10k–50k production-like prompts split by intent buckets.
- gate_event: a defined metric breach that prevents rollout of a cheap_profile.

Spreadsheet layout (recommended columns / rows):
- sheet: profile_calibration_<profile-name> (one sheet per profile)
- columns (each column is a string value in CSV-like cell):
  * prompt_id
  * intent_bucket
  * baseline_output_snippet
  * baseline_score_{metric} (e.g., nDCG_10, exact_match, pass_rate)
  * cheap_output_snippet
  * cheap_score_{metric}
  * delta_{metric} (cheap - baseline)
  * token_count_baseline
  * token_count_cheap
  * latency_ms_baseline_95
  * latency_ms_cheap_95
  * cost_per_call_baseline_usd
  * cost_per_call_cheap_usd
  * flagged_reason (human label: hallucination, omission, quality_drop)
  * human_review_link

Quick formulas (add comment cells):
- avg_delta_metric = AVERAGE(delta_{metric}) for the eval slice.
- p95_latency_delta = p95(latency_ms_cheap) - p95(latency_ms_baseline).
- cost_savings_pct = 1 - (avg cost_per_call_cheap / avg cost_per_call_baseline).
- estimated_monthly_savings = cost_savings_pct * baseline_monthly_spend * adoption_fraction.

Candidate metrics to gate on (examples):
- nDCG@10: tolerable drop <= 0.03 absolute for high-value intent buckets; <= 0.05 for long-tail intents.
- pass_rate (binary correctness): drop <= 0.01 absolute across the whole eval set.
- hallucination_rate: increase <= 0.005 absolute (0.5 percentage points).
- latency_p95: must not exceed baseline_p95 + 120ms for interactive SLO routes.
- cost_delta_per_token: prefer >20% savings to consider gating tradeoffs.

Suggested gate logic (decision tree):
1) Run shadow evaluation on 20k eval prompts (split 80/20 dev/holdout).
2) If avg_delta_nDCG > 0.03 OR hallucination_increase > 0.005, FAIL gate -> no rollout.
3) Else, compute per-intent bucket deltas. If any high-value bucket fails threshold, FAIL gate.
4) If gate passes, run human spot-check: sample 200 prompts stratified by bucket and review. If >5 human-flagged critical regressions, FAIL.
5) If all above pass, allow staged rollout with monitoring and budget cap.

Rollout plan (gradual fallback with budget):
- Stage 0 (internal shadow): 0% traffic, 100% shadow; validation window 48h.
- Stage 1 (canary): 1% traffic, for 24–72h, realtime metrics + notifiers.
- Stage 2 (ramped): 1% -> 5% -> 25% over 7 days if no gate events.
- Stage 3 (fallback-enabled): cheap_profile is allowed to serve when baseline capacity breached; default traffic share still limited by cost/quality guardrails.
- Budget guard: stop progressive ramp if projected monthly cost exceeds baseline * (1 - target_savings_pct) or if observed per-call quality regressions exceed bucket thresholds.

Monitoring and alerting (instrumentation notes):
- Events to emit from runtime per-call: profile_used, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, sampling_seed, request_route.
- Route-level dashboards: per-profile p50/p90/p95 latency, cost per 1k requests, quality proxy metrics (A/B side-by-side eval snippet scoring).
- Alerts (auto): trigger on any of the following during ramp:
  * sudden increase in hallucination_proxy (model outputs with hallucination keywords) > 0.01 absolute in 1h window.
  * p95 latency regression > +200ms for interactive routes.
  * unexpected token cost spike > 30% vs. baseline.

Human evaluation guidelines (short):
- Use blind format: reviewers do not know which output is baseline vs cheap.
- Focus rubric on safety/accuracy for high-value buckets, fluency for general buckets.
- Label categories: Acceptable, Slight regression (non-actionable), Regression (actionable), Safety Issue.
- Keep a small canonical set of 250 prompts that are repeatedly included in calibrations to detect drift.

Practical calibration run example (one-paragraph):
- Profile: 4-bit quant + 4k context truncation on a 7B model. Baseline: 16-bit 32k context. Run: 20k prompts sampled across 8 intents plus 250 canonical prompts. Observed avg nDCG drop = 0.018 (passes), hallucination rate +0.003 (passes), top intent bucket nDCG drop = 0.04 (FAIL for that bucket). Decision: hold rollout, run mitigations (increase beam/temperature tuning for that bucket; try partial quant with cache for heavy prompt types).

Mitigations to try before re-run:
- mixed-mode: quantize only feed-forward layers not attention (reduces quality hit).
- restricted fallback policy: for identified buckets, keep baseline model pinned; for others allow cheap profile.
- prompt prefixing: add short context preservation tokens to reduce truncation harm.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact statistical test and sample size for small buckets (need guidance from stats team).
- How to fold in long-term quality drift into gates (timing windows vs. cumulative stats).
- Add a per-customer sensitivity multiplier for cost thresholds (enterprise customers tolerate less quality regression).

Immediate next steps (owner + timeframe):
- Asha: create template spreadsheet and sample run for 4-bit quant profile by 2024-03-07.
- Miguel: wire up shadow logging events to metrics pipeline by 2024-03-14 (OPT-711).
- Lena: draft human-review rubrics and allocate reviewers by 2024-03-10.

Notes / links to existing artifacts:
- See the eval harness repo for scoring functions and dataset sampling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness
- Related confluence draft: optimize-eval-harness (linked above).
- Jira epic for gate automation: OPT-711.

Quick checklist (copy into PR description when proposing a cheap profile):
- [ ] Spreadsheet with baseline vs cheap outputs for full eval set uploaded
- [ ] Automated metric run completed (nDCG, pass_rate, hallucination_proxy)
- [ ] Human spot-check completed (200 reviews) and results attached
- [ ] Shadow run >= 48h with event logs
- [ ] Rollout plan + stop conditions specified
- [ ] Alerts hooked into oncall channel and paging threshold defined

End of notes.

(Informal fragments below - keep for context)
- remind: conservative thresholds are better than chasing marginal cost % for enterprise customers.
- keep a running doc of profiles that we allow per-customer (some enterprise contracts will opt-out).
- consider adding an "aggressiveness" score to each profile in spreadsheet: {0..10} for how likely ops should allow fallback under load.
